nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$, let $q$ be a natural number and let $\ell$ be a bijection from the edge set of $G$ to $\{0, 1, \dots, q-1\}$. The incident-edge sum at a vertex $v$ is $\sum_{e \ni v} (\ell(e) + 1)$, the sum over the edges $e$ of $G$ that contain $v$; in other words, the edges carry the labels $1, \dots, q$.
nodes.title: Incident-edge sum

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite nonempty vertex set $V$, let $q$ be a natural number and let $\ell$ be a bijection from the edge set of $G$ to $\{0, \dots, q-1\}$. For every vertex $v$, the induced residue of $v$ with respect to $\ell$, read as a natural number, equals the incident-edge sum at $v$ with respect to $\ell$ modulo $|V|$.
nodes.title: Value of the induced residue

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$, let $q$ be a natural number and let $\ell$ be a bijection from the edge set of $G$ to $\{0, \dots, q-1\}$. The induced residue of a vertex $v$ is the incident-edge sum at $v$ (with edge labels $\ell(e) + 1$) reduced modulo $|V|$, viewed as an element of $\{0, \dots, |V| - 1\}$. When $|V| = 0$ there are no vertices, so there is nothing to define.
nodes.title: Induced vertex residue

nodes.summary: A simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set $V$ is edge-graceful if and only if there are a natural number $q$, a bijection $\ell$ from the edge set of $G$ to $\{0, \dots, q-1\}$ and a bijection $\lambda$ from $V$ to $\{0, \dots, |V| - 1\}$ such that for every vertex $v$, $\lambda(v)$ is the induced residue of $v$ with respect to $\ell$ and, if $V$ is nonempty, $\lambda(v)$ equals the incident-edge sum at $v$ with…
nodes.title: Edge-graceful graphs via a vertex bijection

nodes.summary: A simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set $V$ is edge-graceful when there are a natural number $q$ and a bijection $\ell$ from the edge set of $G$ to $\{0, \dots, q-1\}$ such that the induced residue map, sending each vertex $v$ to the sum of $\ell(e) + 1$ over the edges $e$ containing $v$ taken modulo $|V|$, is a bijection from $V$ to $\{0, \dots, |V| - 1\}$.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
